hero.title: Air Freight Customs Clearance Belgium
hero.subtitle: Air freight customs clearance in Belgium requires accurate data, early document checks, and the correct declaration.

intro.p1: Imports are normally processed through IDMS, while PLDA is limited to approved fallback cases. Winz handles <1>EU import declaration service</1> for importers, exporters, freight forwarders, and logistics companies that need compliant air cargo clearance without airport delays. For general customs processes, see <2>customs clearance Belgium</2>.
intro.p2: We prepare declarations, check documents, coordinate customs queries, and confirm release. Airport transport and final delivery remain the responsibility of the importer or logistics provider.

howItClears.title: How Air Cargo Clears Customs
howItClears.intro: Air freight clearance includes pre-loading security filing, import declaration, customs control, and release. Early document preparation can reduce delays, but inspections, warehouse procedures, and airline handling remain outside the customs broker's control.

ics2.title: ICS2 Pre-Loading Filing
ics2.text: Air cargo entering or transiting through the EU requires ICS2 safety and security data. The carrier, freight forwarder, or another supply-chain party may file it. Missing consignee details, vague goods descriptions, or incomplete house shipment data can cause delays.

idms.title: IDMS Import Declaration
idms.text: Winz prepares or pre-lodges the Belgian import declaration using the air waybill, HS code, customs value, EORI number, origin, procedure, duty, and VAT details. IDMS handles standard declarations, while PLDA is limited to approved fallback cases.

control.title: Customs Control
control.text: Belgian customs may release the goods electronically, conduct a documentary or physical inspection, or request additional information. The decision depends on risk analysis, product controls, origin, routing, and declaration data.

release.title: Release or Temporary Storage
release.text: Cargo is released after customs, duty, VAT, guarantee, and inspection requirements are complete. Winz confirms release, while the airline handler or logistics provider manages collection. Unreleased goods may remain in temporary storage or enter transit, customs warehousing, temporary admission, or another approved procedure.

documents.title: Air Freight Documents Required
documents.intro: The air waybill identifies the shipment route, consignor, consignee, airports, and goods. A Master Air Waybill (MAWB) covers the airline's consolidated consignment, while each House Air Waybill (HAWB) identifies an individual shipment that may require a separate customs declaration.

table.purpose: Identifies the shipment and transport reference
Confirms value, currency, goods, and Incoterm
Shows packages, weights, and cargo details

documents.postTable: All documents must show consistent quantities, weights, values, parties, and product details. Vague descriptions such as "parts" or "equipment" should state what the goods are, their material, and use. For the full document set required for air cargo, see <1>customs documents air freight Belgium</1>.
documents.brusselsSupport: Winz handles air freight customs clearance Brussels Airport for Belgian commercial imports and exports.

whatWeNeed.title: What Winz Needs to Start
whatWeNeed.intro: Early document submission gives Winz time to identify missing data before the cargo arrives. The exact requirements depend on the commodity, origin, customs procedure, and importer structure.
whatWeNeed.subtitle: Please provide:
list: The MAWB and all relevant HAWBs
The commercial invoice and packing list
The importer's EORI and VAT details
The commodity code, if already confirmed
The country of origin and dispatch country
The agreed Incoterm
The arrival airport and expected arrival time
Importer, exporter, and consignee details
Origin evidence, licences, or certificates where applicable
Instructions for duty, VAT, deferment, or guarantee use
whatWeNeed.outro: Winz may request additional information where the invoice does not support the declared customs value or commodity classification.

duties.title: Duties, VAT, and Customs Value
duties.text: Import duty depends on the commodity code, customs value, origin, and tariff preference. Belgium's standard VAT rate is 21%, although exceptions apply. Eligible businesses may account for import VAT through ET 14000. Winz verifies the applicable duty and VAT.

representation.title: Customs Representation
representation.text: Direct representation means the broker acts in the trader's name. Under indirect representation, the broker acts in its own name and may share customs-debt liability. Winz confirms the suitable option and required authorisation. Non-EU businesses may also need an EU importer or fiscal structure.

airports.title: Belgian Airport Customs Coverage
airports.intro: Winz supports commercial air cargo declarations through Belgian and nearby European gateways.

brussels.title: Brussels Airport
brussels.text: Winz prepares import and <1>export declaration Belgium</1> for air shipments, checks air waybills and invoices, and coordinates customs queries for pharmaceutical, express, and general cargo. Airport handlers manage cargo availability, handling, and collection release.

liege.title: Liège Airport
liege.text: Where service arrangements are available, Winz supports import, export, transit, and documentation for express, e-commerce, perishable, and general cargo. Send MAWB, HAWB, invoices, packing lists, and arrival details before landing.

schiphol.title: Schiphol Cross-Border Clearance
schiphol.text: Shipments via <1>customs clearance Amsterdam Schiphol</1> use Dutch customs systems. Goods may enter free circulation in the Netherlands or move under transit for clearance elsewhere. Winz confirms the route, EORI requirements, and VAT treatment before filing.

perishable.title: Perishable and Controlled Cargo
perishable.text: <1>Perishable goods air freight Belgium</1> needs early coordination, but only specific regulated goods require Border Control Post checks. These may need pre-notification, TRACES processing, a Common Health Entry Document, certificates, or inspection. Winz handles customs declarations. Importers or specialist agents manage health documentation and inspection arrangements. Customs release does not replace other authority approvals.

dangerous.title: Dangerous Goods Support
dangerous.text: Batteries, chemicals, aerosols, gases, and certain medical products may require specialised packaging, labels, and transport documents. <1>Dangerous goods air freight IATA Belgium</1> classification and packaging requirements must be confirmed before loading at origin. Winz checks customs data. Shippers and qualified transport parties handle dangerous-goods classification, packaging, and airline acceptance. Correct customs codes do not establish air transport compliance.

export.title: Air Freight Export Declarations
export.text: Winz prepares AES export declarations and checks shipment documents, commodity codes, exporter details, value, destination, and procedure. Export release permits departure; exit confirmation supports VAT and compliance records. A separate Exit Summary Declaration may be required where applicable safety and security data is not otherwise covered.

delays.title: Common Causes of Delays
delays.intro: Many airport clearance problems begin with incomplete or inconsistent commercial data. Correcting the information before arrival is usually easier than amending it after customs has selected the shipment for control. Shipments requiring <1>priority customs clearance Belgium</1> should be pre-lodged before the flight arrives to avoid release delays.
delays.subtitle: Common causes include:
list: Vague or incomplete invoice descriptions
Different weights on the AWB and packing list
Missing or invalid EORI information
Incorrect importer or consignee details
Unsupported customs values
Incorrect commodity codes
Missing preferential origin evidence
Incomplete house-level ICS2 data
Missing licences or health certificates
Unclear duty or VAT payment instructions
Cargo not available for inspection
Airline handler or warehouse release restrictions
delays.outro: Winz reviews the available documents and explains which corrections are needed. Customs acceptance and inspection decisions remain with the relevant customs authority. Importers who need to understand <1>how long air freight customs takes</1> should factor in inspection risk, commodity type, and document completeness.

questions.q: What is air freight customs clearance?
questions.a: It is the process used to declare imported or exported air cargo to customs. It can include safety filings, document checks, duty and VAT assessment, licences, customs controls, and release.

questions.q: What is the difference between ICS2 and IDMS?
questions.a: ICS2 handles safety and security data before goods enter or transit through the EU. IDMS is the Belgian system used to submit standard import customs declarations.
Belgium uses IDMS for standard import declarations wherever possible. PLDA remains available only for limited fallback cases, known technical problems, or exceptions accepted by Belgian customs.

Most shipments require an air waybill, commercial invoice, packing list, EORI number, commodity code, and origin information. Controlled goods may also require licences, certificates, or health documents.

questions.q: What is the MAWB and HAWB difference?
questions.a: A MAWB covers the airline’s master consignment. A HAWB identifies an individual shipment inside a consolidated load. Each HAWB may require a separate customs declaration.
There is no fixed clearance time. Timing depends on document quality, customs controls, cargo presentation, duty and VAT arrangements, licences, and airport warehouse procedures.
Yes. Air cargo may remain in temporary storage or move into an authorised customs warehouse after the correct declaration or movement procedure has been completed.
The cargo must be presented to customs. Customs may check the goods, invoice, air waybill, commodity code, origin, quantity, and declared value before confirming release.
Winz focuses on customs clearance. Airport collection and onward delivery are normally arranged by the importer, freight forwarder, or logistics provider.

questions.q: Can Winz clear cargo before arrival?
questions.a: The declaration may be prepared or pre-lodged before arrival where the required data is available, and the customs procedure allows it. Final release still depends on arrival and presentation.
